message: The dataset is the classic Titanic problem. The target column is "Survived" which is binary (0/1), so the task is binary classification. The sample submission contains the id column "PassengerId" and a single prediction column "Survived" with integer values, indicating the required submission format is a label (hard class). The competition does not specify a custom metric, and the usual Kaggle Titanic competition is evaluated by accuracy, which is one of the allowed metrics. The data shows moderate class imbalance (skew 0.48) but not extreme. Main risks are the high missing rate in "Age" (≈20 %) and especially "Cabin" (≈77 %), plus high‑cardinality text fields ("Name", "Ticket", "Cabin") that can cause leakage or over‑fitting if not handled properly. Therefore we will start with tree‑based models that handle missing values and categorical encoding well, plus a linear model as a baseline. The available model families are lightgbm, hist_gb, random_forest, extra_trees, and linear.

message: Titanic data has several high‑cardinality text fields that risk leakage if used raw. We extract the informative parts with regex: Title from Name, TicketPrefix from Ticket, and CabinLetter from Cabin. These reduce cardinality and capture known survival signals (e.g., titles, deck). After extraction we drop the original raw columns to avoid over‑fitting. Fare is heavily right‑skewed (skew 4.79) so we log‑transform it. Ticket and Cabin still have many distinct values; we add frequency encoding for them to give the model a numeric prevalence signal. Groups defined by TicketPrefix and CabinLetter often appear in both train and test (test_seen_pct > 30% for Ticket, >10% for Cabin) and passengers sharing a prefix or deck plausibly share survival outcomes, so we add group‑target encoding (mean target of other group members) with a small smoothing of 1 and a minimum group size of 2. We also add group‑size columns for these keys to give the model size information. Missing indicators are kept (default true). No datetime columns exist, and we do not need text length features after extracting the key parts. The target is binary, so we do not log‑transform it.

message: The dataset is small (891 rows, 17 features) so we favour stronger regularisation to avoid over‑fitting. We propose two LightGBM configs: a baseline (moderate n_estimators, learning_rate, num_leaves) and a more regularised version (lower learning_rate, fewer leaves, higher min_child_samples, slightly higher reg_lambda). A HistGradientBoosting model provides a different boosting implementation with moderate max_iter and default leaf size. Finally a linear model (logistic regression) adds a low‑bias, high‑variance‑complementary learner for the ensemble. With 4 experiments we set ensemble_top_k=2, which will run greedy selection over the best 4 models, encouraging a diverse yet strong ensemble.

Random Forest and Extra Trees are introduced to increase model diversity for the ensemble. All configurations respect the provided param_space and avoid duplication of previous experiments. ensemble_top_k is set to 2 so the greedy ensemble will consider the top 4 new models.
